questions.problem: What is the projection of the intersection between the hyperboloid of two sheets $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{8}=-1$ and the plane $y=2$ onto the $xz$-plane?
questions.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the hyperboloid and the plane $y=2$, we substitute $y=2$ into the equation of the hyperboloid:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(2)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{8} & =-1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}+1-\frac{{z}^{2}}{8} & =-1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{8} & =-2 \\ -\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{16} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the hyperbola: $-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{16}=1.$

questions.problem: Given the hyperboloid of one sheet  $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-\frac{(z-1)^{2}}{5}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
questions.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-\frac{(z-1)^{2}}{5} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-1 & =\frac{(z-1)^{2}}{5} \\ (z-1)^{2} & =5(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-1) \\ (z-1) & =\pm \sqrt{5(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

  

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}-1 & \ge 0 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8} & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the exterior of the ellipse $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}=1$, including its boundary.

Therefore, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{8}\ge 1\}.
$$

questions.problem: The projection of the intersection between the hyperboloid of two sheets $\frac{5(x-1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{5(y-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(z-3)^{2}}{4}=-1$ and the plane $z=2$ onto the $xy$-plane is a hyperbola. What are the lengths of the semi-axes of the hyperbola?
questions.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the hyperboloid and the plane $z=2$, we substitute $z=2$ into the equation of the hyperboloid:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5(x-1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{5(y-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(2-3)^{2}}{4} & =-1 \\ \frac{5(x-1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{5(y-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{1}{4} & =-1 \\ \frac{5(x-1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{5(y-2)^{2}}{16} & =-1-\frac{1}{4} \\ \frac{5(x-1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{5(y-2)^{2}}{16} & =-\frac{5}{4} \\ -(x-1)^{2}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ -\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{{1}^{2}}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of a hyperbola with semi-axes of lengths $1$ and $2.$

questions.problem: What is the projection of the intersection between the hyperboloid of one sheet $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{8}+{z}^{2}=1$ and the plane $z=1$ onto the $xy$-plane?
questions.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the hyperboloid and the plane $z=1$, we substitute $z=1$ into the equation of the hyperboloid:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{8}+{1}^{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{8}+1 & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{8} & =0 \\ {y}^{2} & =4(x-2)^{2} \\ y & =\pm 2(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two intersecting lines: $y=2(x-2)$ and $y=-2(x-2).$

questions.problem: Given the hyperboloid of one sheet $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+(y-1)^{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{16}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
questions.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+(y-1)^{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+(y-1)^{2}-1 & =\frac{{z}^{2}}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2} & =16(\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+(y-1)^{2}-1) \\ z & =\pm 4\sqrt{\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+(y-1)^{2}-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+(y-1)^{2}-1 & \ge 0 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+(y-1)^{2} & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the exterior of the ellipse $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+(y-1)^{2}=1,$ which includes the boundary.

Therefore, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\,:\,\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+(y-1)^{2}\ge 1\}.
$$
